clue.text: Messed up patrol car by arresting chap from stag do

indicators.note: something messed up has been thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled
to arrest someone is to seize and hold them, so one part takes the other inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be jumbled
a chap is a he, a male

explanation.surface: Police officers wreck their car while hauling a reveller away from a rowdy stag night.
explanation.walkthrough: HE goes inside the fodder first, then all thirteen letters are rearranged into BACHELOR PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag do is the British name for the pre-wedding celebration a groom holds with his male friends.

clue.text: Openings in Associated Press and, unusually, Reuters

indicators.note: done unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: AP is the standard abbreviation of the news agency
the news agency's name rearranged

explanation.surface: A media story about vacancies or opportunities found at two big news agencies.
explanation.definitionFit: Apertures are gaps or holes, so they are openings in the physical sense.

clue.text: Haul up last case into hold

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word that follows it
one thing put into another sits inside it

blocks.note: to hold something is to have it
final letter of case

explanation.surface: Dockers hoist the final crate up into a ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' looks like a ship's cargo space, but it is the verb meaning have.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to lift or haul something heavy with great effort.

clue.text: Illuminated tulip sculpture

indicators.note: a sculpture is something shaped and modelled, so the letters are moulded into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A floodlit statue of a flower, as in a gallery or park display.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lit up has light shining on it, which is what illuminated means.

clue.text: Carpet has nap woven round edge, all in scarlet

indicators.note: threads that are woven are twisted together, so the letters are interlaced in a new order
going round something means surrounding it, so one part wraps another
everything built so far is placed inside the next word

blocks.note: scarlet is a shade of red
the word nap rearranged
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A description of a rug: its pile is woven with a red border all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' reads as a rug with nap, but it is the verb meaning to scold, as a boss summons someone onto the carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is a British informal idiom for summoning and scolding them, which is to reprimand.

clue.text: Heavenly being in Russian port

blocks.note: first meaning: a chief angel
second meaning: the northern Russian city on the White Sea, also called Arkhangelsk

explanation.surface: An angelic figure turns up in a Russian harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: An archangel is an angel of high rank, and Archangel is the English name of a White Sea port.

clue.text: Attempt to speak to commercial society in China

indicators.note: speaking means saying it out loud, so what counts is the sound and not the spelling

blocks.note: an attempt is a try; spelt to match its sound
a commercial is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: Someone tries to address a trade association in China.
explanation.definitionFit: A triad is a Chinese secret society, often associated with organised crime.

clue.text: Respected opinion held by liberated fellow

indicators.note: something liberated is set free, so the letters are released from their order
a thing held by another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: the word fellow rearranged, split around the middle
a thought is an opinion

explanation.surface: A freed prisoner's views are given a respectful hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-thought-of is held in high regard, so esteemed by others.

clue.text: Original Westerns had to be agreeably brief

indicators.note: something original is newly made, so these letters are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: with the following 'to', taken as written as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A film critic's rule: the classic cowboy films had to be kept tight and punchy.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is 'Westerns had to'; 'to' does double work as the end of the fodder, leaving 'be' to join.
explanation.definitionFit: Short and sweet is an idiom for something pleasantly concise, not dragged out.

clue.text: Brief lament by worker's in good taste

indicators.note: making something brief means cutting it short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: an elegy is a poem of mourning, a lament
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A short sad poem written by a labourer turns out to be tasteful.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant describes something graceful and stylish, showing refinement.

clue.text: A bit hungry, becoming sick and hot after exercise

indicators.note: becoming means turning into something else, so the letters change their order
after sets the order: the rest is placed behind the exercise piece

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
the word sick rearranged
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: After a workout someone feels peckish but also queasy and overheated.
explanation.definitionFit: Peckish is a British informal word for slightly hungry, wanting a snack.

clue.text: Girl at teashop has some coffee

indicators.note: having some of something means holding only a part of it, so the letters sit inside the words

blocks.note: found across girL AT TEashop

explanation.surface: A young woman in a tea room orders a coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is an espresso drink made with lots of steamed milk.

clue.text: Flirt makes boy with romantic heart turn red

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters count
to turn something round is to face it the other way, so it is written backwards

blocks.note: Phil is a boy's name
the two central letters of romantic
the word red written backwards

explanation.surface: A lad's romantic heart makes him blush when he flirts.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to have casual affairs or flirt with many partners, used as a verb.

clue.text: Brave man died for old king

blocks.note: a hero is a brave man
D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A courageous man gave his life for an ancient monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod was the biblical King of Judea, a ruler from ancient times.

clue.text: Heavyweight paper's turned on Israeli leader with article that's really harsh

indicators.note: something turned is facing the opposite way, so it is read backwards
the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: card is thick, heavy paper; written backwards
taken as written
first letter of Israeli
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A heavyweight newspaper turns on an Israeli prime minister with a scathing piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavyweight paper' suggests a broadsheet newspaper, but it is card, the stiff kind of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian means excessively severe, after Draco, the strict lawgiver of ancient Athens.

clue.text: Treatment of a gland that's died off's reportedly easier when feeling no pain

definitions.note: a phrase describing the state; the answer is the noun naming it

indicators.note: off means taken away, so that letter is removed
treating something works it over, so these letters are processed into a new order
reported means passed on by word of mouth, so the sound counts

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for died; this letter is removed
said without the final r, as in southern English speech

explanation.surface: Medical treatment for a dead gland is said to be easier when the patient cannot feel pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Take D out of A GLAND, rearrange the rest, then add the ending -ESIA, which in British speech sounds like easier.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the medical term for the absence or relief of pain.

clue.text: Graduate's taken up house last owner let get disgusting

indicators.note: in a down entry, taken up means lifted upwards, so it reads bottom to top
last points to the final letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, a graduate, written backwards
HO is an abbreviation for house
final letter of owner
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A graduate moved into a house that the previous landlord left in a revolting state.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means inspiring loathing, so repugnant or revolting.

clue.text: Told wrong procedure regarding grammatical rules

indicators.note: something told is spoken aloud, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a wrong is a sin; spelt to match its sound
a tactic is a method or procedure

explanation.surface: Someone was informed they had followed the wrong process.
explanation.definitionFit: Syntactic relates to syntax, the rules governing how words combine into sentences.

clue.text: Animal found in a French outhouse is safe and sound

indicators.note: a thing found in another is located inside it

blocks.note: un is French for a
a shed is an outhouse
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: A missing pet discovered in a French garden shed is unhurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Unscathed means without harm or injury, which is what safe and sound expresses.

clue.text: Fitted with inner sleeve that's creased

blocks.note: first meaning: given an inner covering, as a coat or pipe
second meaning: marked with wrinkles, as a face

explanation.surface: A garment with a lining that has become crumpled.
explanation.definitionFit: Lined means having a lining layer inside, and also marked with lines or wrinkles.

clue.text: Sheltered boy, taking year out before university, about to enter tough environment

indicators.note: taking out removes something, here the abbreviation for year
before fixes the order, putting one piece ahead of the next
entering means going inside, so this group sits within the outer word

blocks.note: hard means tough; as an environment it forms the outer shell
taken as written; Y for year is removed
U is the abbreviation for university
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A gap-year student is given refuge in a rough neighbourhood before going to college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking year out' evokes a gap year, but it means removing the abbreviation Y from boy; 'environment' says the tough word surrounds the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour someone is to give them shelter or refuge, so harboured means sheltered.

clue.text: Artist to get figure in proportion

indicators.note: to get something in is to take it inside, so the figure is placed within

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one, a figure

explanation.surface: A painter is told to draw a figure with correct proportions.
explanation.walkthrough: The container signal is 'get ... in', with TO taking I inside; 'figure in proportion' reads like art-class advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the relative size of two quantities, which is a proportion.

clue.text: Clobber needs to be packed

indicators.note: to clobber something is to batter it, knocking the letters into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Gear or clothing has to be packed into a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like the British slang noun for clothes or gear, but here it is the verb to bash.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense means closely compacted, with its parts tightly crammed together.

clue.text: Overacting lead in West End review gets catcall

indicators.note: to re-view is to look again, here from the opposite direction, reading backwards
the lead of a word is its opening letter
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for west
an end is an aim or goal
first letter of overacting

explanation.surface: A hammy lead actor in a London theatre show gets jeered by a critic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' reads as London's theatre district, but it splits into W and an end meaning goal. Catcall is taken literally: a cat's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Miaow is the sound a cat makes, so literally a call by a cat.

clue.text: Powerful man takes challenge on the ski slopes

blocks.note: first meaning: a magnate, an important and influential person
second meaning: a mound of hard snow on a ski run

explanation.surface: A strong man tackles a tough run while skiing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mogul is a tycoon, and also a bump formed on ski pistes that skiers must negotiate.

clue.text: Briefly describe an unfashionable design?

blocks.note: out means no longer in fashion
a line is a fashion designer's range or design

explanation.surface: A request to sum up a dated fashion design in a few words.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'unfashionable design' is a playful split: a range of clothes that is out.
explanation.definitionFit: To outline is to give a summary covering only the main points.

clue.text: Close fastener on lingerie

blocks.note: nigh means near, close
a tie is something that fastens

explanation.surface: Doing up a clasp on a piece of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like the verb to shut, but it is the adjective meaning near.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, which counts among lingerie, women's nightwear and underwear.

clue.text: Where hands work day and night?

definitions.text: Where hands work day and night?

blocks.clueFragment: Where hands work day and night?
blocks.note: surface reading: a place where labourers toil on shifts without stopping
setter's reading: the hands are those of a clock face, which move continually through all hours

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' suggests workers in a factory; the clock's hands literally go round its face all day and night.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means continuously, all day and all night, and is literally where a clock's hands travel.
